newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds move lower, seen continuing down.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds move lower, seen continuing down.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds turned lower on Monday in lacklustre trading with no domestic players and few foreigners seen in the market, and traders said they expected the gentle downtrend to continue.

"It will keep going down. There are no domestic buyers, foreigners are getting turned off by the politicial scandals and funding is getting very expensive so you don't want to hold the 2000 (maturity)," one trader said.
However, traders noted that market volumes were very thin and that it did not take much to knock the bonds lower. They said they expected little before Friday's U.S. jobs figures.
The bond market barely reacted to slightly stronger than expected figures from the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Managers on Monday.
"The more important figure is on Friday. I don't expect much movement before then," one trader said.

He said there was an underlying worry - but no panic - because of the political bribery scandals that are sapping the coalition government's strength, although there was a feeling that there were more to come.
"No one is panicking, although in my opinion people should panic," the trader said.
The announced closure of French carmaker Renault's plant at Vilvoorde in Belgium that sent some 4,000 demonstrators onto the streets of Brussels on Monday had no impact on the bond market.
"It is industrial. It has not got through to the political level so there is no impact on bonds," one trader said.
However, traders said the markets would be keeping a weather eye on developments just in case Belgium's growing industrial discontent did grow and spill over into the political sphere.
Traders noted that the 2003 and 2004 maturities stood out on Monday, being quoted relatively lower than the rest of the market after being historically expensive compared to Germany.
The yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO was 5.66 percent at the close of business on Monday, unchanged from Friday. The spread over Bunds was 11 basis points against Friday's 15.
The March futures contract was 26 basis points down at 122.86.
